chunks: Now then, I advise you to fear Allah, Who created you for the first time,
towards Him is your return, with Him lies the success of your aims, at Him terminate (all) your desires, towards Him runs your path of right and He is the aim of your fears (for seeking protection).

Certainly, fear of Allah is the medicine for the sickness of your hearts, sight for the blindness of your spirits, the cure for the ailments of your bodies, the rectifier of the evils of your breasts, the purifier of the pollution of your minds, the light of the darkness of your eyes, the consolation for the fear of your heart and the brightness for the gloom of your ignorance.

key_terms.تَقْوَى: God-consciousness or piety, the central theme of the exhortation
key_terms.جَأْشِكُمْ: Your heart/inner self (specifically regarding fear or agitation)
key_terms.مَعَادُكُمْ: Your return or destination (in the Hereafter)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits and metaphors for Taqwa (fear of God) in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from his famous sermon, Imam Ali (AS) employs a rich rhetorical structure of parallelism to define Taqwa not merely as fear, but as a comprehensive spiritual cure (dawa') for the heart's blindness and the soul's impurity. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on Taqwa as an active, internal state of awareness that governs both metaphysical return (ma'ad) and practical success in worldly endeavors. The description aligns with the concept of 'Ihsan' (spiritual excellence) where God-consciousness illuminates the inner self against the darkness of negligence.
